spans.text: At one time the Buddha was staying near Mithilā in the Maghadeva Mango Grove.
Rañño kho panānanda, maghadevassa puttapaputtakā tassa paramparā caturāsītirājasahassāni imasmiṁyeva maghadevaambavane kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajiṁsu.

entries.description: The people of Videha are so fortunate
entries.subject: The people

spans.text: ‘lābhā vata, bho, videhānaṁ, suladdhaṁ vata, bho, videhānaṁ, ‘The people of Videha are so fortunate, so very fortunate abhiruheyyāsi, mahārāja, dibbaṁ yānaṁ avikampamāno’ti.
King Nimi consented with silence.
Then, knowing that the king had consented, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, Sakka vanished from King Nimi and reappeared among the gods of the thirty-three.
Atha kho, ānanda, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṁse āmantesi: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed the gods of the thirty-three, ‘iccheyyātha no tumhe, mārisā, nimiṁ rājānaṁ daṭṭhun’ti?

Atha kho, ānanda, sakko devānamindo mātaliṁ saṅgāhakaṁ āmantesi: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed his chariot handler Mātali, ‘ehi tvaṁ, samma mātali, sahassayuttaṁ ājaññarathaṁ yojetvā nimiṁ rājānaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadehi— ‘Come, dear Mātali, harness the chariot with a thousand thoroughbreds.
Then go to King Nimi and say, ayaṁ te, mahārāja, sahassayutto ājaññaratho sakkena devānamindena pesito; “Great king, this chariot has been sent for you by Sakka, lord of gods.
He did as Sakka asked, and said to the king, ‘ayaṁ te, mahārāja, sahassayutto ājaññaratho sakkena devānamindena pesito; ‘Great king, this chariot has been sent for you by Sakka, lord of gods.
Tena kho pana, ānanda, samayena nimi rājā tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṁnhāto uposathiko uparipāsādavaragato nisinno hoti.
